Hi Logan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security review team had a couple of follow-ups specifically on your hosted API behavior around geo snapshots/backups and tenant erasure:

1) Can you summarize where data is stored (primary + backups) when we choose a US region? Are backups replicated to other regions?
2) What are the default retention windows for request logs, embedding vectors, and persistent customer blobs (attachments, files) and how are those enforced?
3) If we request a tenant-level erasure, what is the end-to-end timeline and what systems are affected (DB rows, backups, analytics, cache, logs)? Do you provide deletion certificates or evidence?

Appreciate a concise runbook we can attach to our questionnaire. If possible, include the maximum time until all customer data is removed from recoverable state (not just deleted flags).

Hi Sophie —

Thanks — good questions. Summary below; I kept it high level and attached a short runbook + diagram that maps the systems. If you want more detail we can open a technical deep dive with Neha.

Where data lives (US region):
- Primary serving: customer requests and generated model output are processed in the US region you select (e.g., us-east-1).
- Short-term storage: ephemeral request buffers and KV cache live on local instance SSDs and are treated as ephemeral (default TTL 30 minutes).
- Persistent stores: logs, embeddings, and persisted blobs are stored in encrypted object storage in the same selected region by default.
- Backups/snapshots: we take periodic point-in-time snapshots of persistent stores. By default snapshots are retained in the same region; cross-region replication is disabled unless you explicitly enable multi-region DR.

Default retention windows (hosted API):
- Request debug logs (text traces): default retention 30 days; configurable to shorter via plan.
- Generation payloads (user prompts + model outputs stored for debugging/quality): 90 days by default; configurable on enterprise plans.
- Embeddings and derived vectors: 90 days by default; if you persist embeddings to our managed vector store they follow the same retention as persisted blobs.
- Persistent customer blobs (attachments/files): 365 days by default; can be set shorter on contract.

Tenant erasure (high-level):
- Initiation: customer submits an erasure request via the Support portal or security contact (we create a JIRA-OPS ticket).
- Identification: ops identifies all tenant identifiers (tenant_id, external ids) across services (DB, object storage, analytics, backups).
- Erasure steps: 1) Mark tenant data as deleted in primary DB, 2) Issue background purge job that removes PII from annotated columns, 3) Trigger object storage lifecycle DELETE for blobs, 4) Remove embeddings and cached vectors, 5) Purge relevant logs and traces within the retention window, 6) Start hard-delete of eligible snapshots/backups per retention policy.
- Timeline: active deletion across primary stores typically completes within 48 hours; purge from backups/snapshots depends on snapshot retention—worst case up to retention window unless you have contracted accelerated purge (see runbook).
- Evidence: we provide a deletion confirmation packet (ticket audit, manifest of removed S3 keys, and ops notes). We can deliver a deletion certificate on enterprise agreements.

Attachments: geo-retention-diagram.png (system map), tenant_erase_runbook.pdf (procedural steps, escalation contacts, and timelines).

I cc'd Neha to add any technical caveats around backups, immutable snapshots, and KMS key rotations.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie, Logan — quick technical clarifications to complement Logan's summary:

1) Snapshots & backups:
- Application-level snapshots (DB snapshots) are incremental and stored in the same region by default. Snapshots taken for backup purposes are immutable for their retention window (we do not alter historical snapshots); however, we support an expedited snapshot purge on enterprise plans where we schedule a removal job to delete snapshot objects and related manifests.
- For immutable storage (WORM) or long-term archival, we treat those separately and require explicit customer consent to store outside the selected region.

2) Hard delete vs logical delete:
- Our standard pipeline marks records as deleted immediately (logical delete) and then triggers asynchronous hard-delete workers.
- Hard-delete removes PII from columns and deletes S3 objects (we overwrite metadata and then remove the object key). For encrypted objects, we also rotate and retire the KMS key if requested, which makes prior backups unrecoverable. Key rotation is an additional control and can accelerate unrecoverability.

3) Backups & replication:
- Cross-region replication is opt-in. If enabled, replication metadata is recorded and the erasure job ensures replicated copies are removed as part of the purge. We maintain an inventory to track replication targets.

4) Logs & analytics:
- Raw ingestion logs are retained per the retention window. Aggregated analytics (metric rollups) are kept for 13 months by default but are not considered PII in most cases; if you require removal we can scrub relevant keys and associated rollups on request.

5) Proof of deletion:
- We produce a manifest: list of object keys deleted, DB tables/primary keys affected, and ops runbook references. We can include checksums if needed. For legal evidence we provide a signed PDF certificate.

Operational note: accelerated erasure (remove snapshots/backups immediately) requires a support/ops window and is subject to an SLA in the enterprise contract.

-Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie —

Answers to your follow-ups:

1) Worst-case for cross-region replication enabled:
- If replication is enabled, the erasure workflow targets primary and replica stores. Worst-case timeline for all recoverable copies to be removed is the active snapshot retention window plus our standard purge scheduling: typically up to 30 days for snapshot manifests plus up to 90 days if you have older long-retention snapshots—so worst-case 120 days. Note: with the accelerated purge add-on we can schedule targeted snapshot object deletions and key rotation to reduce this to <=7 days for most affected objects.

2) Deletion certificate contents:
- Yes — the deletion certificate will include: signed ticket reference (JIRA-OPS-1284), timestamped manifest of deleted S3 keys, list of DB tables and PKs processed, and ops notes. We include a signature from our security team.

3) Accelerated purge add-on:
- Available as a billable add-on on enterprise plans. Typical lead time: 5 business days to schedule the ops window; emergency expedited requests can be considered with 48–72 hour notice subject to approvals.

Next steps: I will attach a shortened version of the runbook for your procurement and open JIRA-OPS-1284 (will share link). If you'd like a 30-minute call to confirm the technical checklist, Neha is available tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
